<h2 id="why-palatinus-isnt-just-another-budapest-bath-the-pala-vibe">Why Palatinus Isnât Just Another Budapest Bath (The âPalaâ Vibe)</h2>
<p>Budapestâs famous baths, SzÃ©chenyi, GellÃ©rt, Rudas, are grand, historic, and a little formal. If GellÃ©rt was on your list: <strong><a href="/gellert-thermal-bath-relaxing-in-elegance-enjoy-the-art-nouveau-architecture-and-soothing-waters-of-this-famous-thermal-bath/">GellÃ©rt Thermal Bath</a> closed in October 2025 for a renovation of about 20 billion Ft and isnât expected back until 2028</strong>, which makes decent year-round alternatives like Palatinus more useful than ever. Palatinus itself sits in the middle of <a href="/margaret-island-budapest/">Margaret Island</a>, a car-free green strip in the Danube, and that location does half the work. You get off the bus, walk into the park, and the city noise just falls away.</p>
<p>Itâs got real history behind it too. Palatinus opened in 1919 as a simple riverbank beach, grew into a proper lido by 1921, and was the first bath in Budapest to offer outdoor bathing at all. Itâs expanded plenty since then, but it still has that old-school lido feel mixed in with the modern slides and wave machine. Locals bring their kids here, their visiting friends, their whole Saturday. Itâs less a tourist attraction than a seasonal ritual generations of Budapesters have kept up.</p>
<h2 id="what-to-expect-on-your-visit-to-palatinus-strand">What to expect on your visit to Palatinus Strand</h2>
<p>Getting there means a short trip to the mostly car-free Margaret Island, which is part of the fun.</p>
<h3 id="getting-there-navigating-to-margaret-islands-gem">Getting There: Navigating to Margaret Islandâs Gem</h3>
<p><strong>Bus 26</strong> is the easiest route: it runs the length of Margaret Island with a âPalatinus fÃ¼rdÅâ stop right at the entrance. Catch it from Nyugati pÃ¡lyaudvar or ÃrpÃ¡d hÃ­d metro station. Or take <strong>Tram 4 or 6</strong> (the cityâs busiest, running 24/7) to the âMargitszigetâ stop at the foot of Margaret Bridge, then either walk 15-20 minutes through the park or hop Bus 26 from there. The BudapestGO app is useful for live departures.</p>
<p>Once youâre on the island, cars are restricted and everyone gets around on foot, rented bikes, or multi-person pedal carts. It reads as an escape from the first step.</p>
<h3 id="first-impressions--navigating-the-complex">First Impressions & Navigating the Complex</h3>
<p>The entrance can feel like a bottleneck on a busy day, but once youâre through, the scale of the place becomes obvious: multiple pool zones, big lawns, food stalls spread across the whole complex. On a peak weekend, the lawns further from the main pools usually have more room for a towel.</p>
<p>Get familiar with the <strong>cashless system</strong> fast. You get a waterproof, touchless top-up wristband (or you can tap your own contactless card at most stalls) for everything inside, food, drinks, extras. No soggy banknotes, which is genuinely nice, and checking the balance before a second lÃ¡ngos avoids surprises.</p>

<h2 id="the-main-attraction-pools-slides-and-soaking-up-the-sun-at-palatinus">The Main Attraction: Pools, Slides, and Soaking Up the Sun at Palatinus</h2>
<p>The pool and slide descriptions below cover the summer offering. They are not a list of what is open right now; use the current operating notice above when planning an autumn visit.</p>
<p>This is the actual point of Palatinus: 11 outdoor pools plus an indoor wellness section, covering pretty much every mood and every age.</p>
<p><picture><source type="image/webp" srcset="/images/optimized/cebfbc0f78f0dae36cb2f40c-400.webp 400w, /images/optimized/cebfbc0f78f0dae36cb2f40c-768.webp 768w, /images/optimized/cebfbc0f78f0dae36cb2f40c-1024.webp 1024w" sizes="(max-width: 756px) calc(100vw - 2.3rem), 720px"><img src="/images/2026/09/palatinus-strand-lido-pools-lawn-overview.jpg" alt="Overview of the outdoor pools and sunbathing lawn at Palatinus Strand" width="1024" height="768" decoding="async" loading="lazy"></picture>
<em>Photo: <a href="https://www.palatinusstrand.hu/">Palatinus StrandfÃ¼rdÅ</a></em></p>
<h3 id="pool-paradise-something-for-everyone">Pool Paradise: Something for Everyone</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>The Wave Pool:</strong> Palatinusâs signature feature. Roughly every hour a bell rings and the waves kick off, and it turns into happy chaos, people bobbing, kids shrieking, everyone grinning. The waves have real force behind them, so hold onto your sunglasses. Usually running from mid-June.</li>
<li><strong>Childrenâs Pools:</strong> Genuinely family-first design here. Shallow pools for toddlers, small slides and play features, and an indoor kidsâ pool (32-34Â°C). Playgrounds are scattered around the site too. Many families spend the whole day here.</li>
<li><strong>Adventure & Leisure Pools (three of them):</strong> The open-air bath pool and the adventure pool run neck showers, bubble beds, and gentle currents for a calmer splash. Two of the three typically open from mid to late May. These are a calmer choice when the wave pool gets too much.</li>
<li><strong>Swimming Pool:</strong> A proper 40-meter lap pool (26Â°C) for people who want actual laps in. <strong>Swim caps are mandatory</strong> here, so bring your own or buy one on site (2,100 HUF on the operatorâs price list).</li>
<li><strong>Thermal Pools (three outdoor, three indoor):</strong> This is where the âbathâ half of Palatinus shows up. The water is rich in calcium-magnesium hydrocarbonate and genuinely soothing. The outdoor âRound poolâ (the MargarÃ©ta, 30-32Â°C) is seasonal; two more seasonal outdoor thermal pools (30-32Â°C and 33-36Â°C) open around late May. The <strong>indoor wellness area</strong>, renovated in 2017, is what makes Palatinus a real year-round option: a thermal leisure pool (36Â°C), a cold plunge (18-20Â°C), a hot plunge pool (40-42Â°C), and the indoor kidsâ pool.</li>
</ul>
<p><picture><source type="image/webp" srcset="/images/optimized/cc05ad5c04176fdd12040761-400.webp 400w, /images/optimized/cc05ad5c04176fdd12040761-768.webp 768w, /images/optimized/cc05ad5c04176fdd12040761-1024.webp 1024w" sizes="(max-width: 756px) calc(100vw - 2.3rem), 720px"><img src="/images/2026/09/palatinus-strand-mural-pool-slides.jpg" alt="The deep-water pool at Palatinus with its painted mural wall and the slide chutes behind" width="1024" height="682" decoding="async" loading="lazy"></picture>
<em>Photo: <a href="https://www.palatinusstrand.hu/">Palatinus StrandfÃ¼rdÅ</a></em></p>
<h3 id="slide-central-for-the-thrill-seekers-and-the-not-so-brave">Slide Central: For the Thrill-Seekers (and the Not-So-Brave)</h3>
<p>The slide tower is a big draw for older kids and adults who never grew out of it. The main slides:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Magic Tunnel:</strong> Medium difficulty, ride it on a tyre (two-seaters available), with colored light effects inside the tunnel. Long at 130m, and good fun with a friend.</li>
<li><strong>Anaconda:</strong> An open, winding slide, also medium, a classic 108m glide.</li>
<li><strong>Kamikaze:</strong> Shortest at 36m, steepest, rated hard. Big splash, quick thrill, no buildup.</li>
<li><strong>Turbo:</strong> Highest starting point (15.6m), rated hard, a fast 60m drop.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Slide rules:</strong> minimum height 120cm, not recommended for pregnant visitors or people with certain health conditions, and adults must supervise anyone under 14. Opening hours

Tickets currently can be booked 6 months in advance, please note that opening times may vary slightly. 

On October 23 the bath will be open from 8 am to 22 pm, the DaysPalm will be open until 2 pm.
On 30 October the Dayspalm is open until 5 pm.

The bath is open from 8 am on holidays and peak season (October 23-25, 2025, December 18, 2026 - January 6, 2027).
On December 25, 2026 and January 1, 2027 the bath is open until 8 pm.

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">We visit Széchenyi Baths early on a freezing cold winter’s morning. It’s surprisingly busy, given it’s early January, and Budapest is still getting back on its feet after years of quieter travel.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The baths are one of <a href="https://www.thecommonwanderer.com/blog/things-to-do-in-budapest-hungary" target="_blank">Budapest’s most popular attractions</a>, built in 1913 over healing hot springs feeding 18 separate pools, 3 outdoor and 15 indoor, and a range of other wellness features including steam rooms and saunas, in the ornate complex.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">After a mad dash from the changing rooms, we sink our chilly bodies into the steaming baths. It’s a sensation unlike any other - tingles over every inch of our skin as our bodies slowly acclimatise to 38 degrees of pure heaven.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The morning sun illuminates the weathered yet grandiose neo-Baroque and neo-Renaissance baths, as billowing steam slowly floats from the pools.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">We sink deeper into the water, delighting in the therapeutic waters while watching the baths slowly fill up. There are the old ladies, enjoying their prescribed ‘natural therapies’ or balneotherapy (it’s a thing here in Hungary!). There’s the man, lounging on the steps, deeply engrossed in a novel. There’s the group, presumably talking about Hungary’s questionable politics. And there are the tourists, standing out like a beacon with their phones, snapping memories of this Insta-famous hotspot.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">It’s a microcosm of everyday Budapest. A city of fading grandeur where citizens, despite their tumultuous past, revel in the good life. A city where politics is whispered under the noses of unsuspecting tourists flitting from gorgeous attraction to gorgeous attraction.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">And it’s bloody wonderful.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">As we make our way from pool to pool, sauna to the steam room, we can’t help but delight in the glory that is Széchenyi baths. Despite all we’d read and seen online, it’s so much more than we expected.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">A <a href="https://www.getyourguide.com/budapest-l29/szechenyi-spa-full-day-entrance-pass-t4139/?cmp=Szechenyi_Guide&partner_id=C8WLDEM&placement=content-middle&utm_medium=online_publisher" target="_blank">visit </a>to Szechenyi baths is truly one of the best <a href="https://www.thecommonwanderer.com/blog/things-to-do-in-budapest-hungary" target="_blank">things to do in Budapest</a>. In fact, it’s so great, you should plan to visit more than once, to really soak it all in (yes, that is a pun!). </p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">To help you plan your visit, our Szechenyi Baths guide will run through everything you need to know before you visit.</p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">ps. Want to explore more of Budapest? Read our in-depth guides here | <a href="https://www.thecommonwanderer.com/blog/gellert-baths-budapest-guide" target="_blank">Gellert Thermal Baths</a>, <a href="https://www.thecommonwanderer.com/blog/szimpla-kert-budapest" target="_blank">Szimpla Kert Ruin Bar</a>, <a href="https://www.thecommonwanderer.com/blog/new-york-cafe-budapest-review" target="_blank">New York Cafe</a>, <a href="https://www.thecommonwanderer.com/blog/best-brunch-budapest" target="_blank">Budapest’s best brunch spots</a>, and <a href="https://www.thecommonwanderer.com/blog/a-guide-to-jozsefvaros-budapest-8th-district" target="_blank">the best of Józsefváros, Budapest’s hipster 8th district</a></p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><blockquote><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><em>LOVE OUR PHOTOS? Edit like us with our </em><a href="https://thecommonwanderer.shop/collections/lightroom-presets/products/european-summer-desktop-mobile-preset-pack" target="_blank"><em>European Summers Preset Packs</em></a><em>, and </em><a href="https://thecommonwanderer.shop/collections/video-filters/products/european-summer-mobile-video-filters" target="_blank"><em>mobile video filters</em></a><em>, inspired by the warm hues and vibes of summers spent in Europe</em></p></blockquote><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p></div>

><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><strong>WHERE |</strong> City Park (Városliget), Budapest<br><strong>HOW TO GET THERE |</strong> M1 Metro to <em>Széchenyi fürdő</em> station, or walk via Heroes’ Square<br><strong>ENTRY |</strong> Weekdays HUF 11,900 / Weekends HUF 13,500 (≈ €30–34) Buy advanced tickets <a href="https://www.getyourguide.com/budapest-l29/szechenyi-spa-full-day-entrance-pass-t4139/?cmp=Szechenyi_Guide&partner_id=C8WLDEM&placement=content-middle&utm_medium=online_publisher" target="_blank">here</a><br><strong>HOURS |</strong> 6 am – 10 pm (daily; indoor pools close 8 pm)<br><strong>TIPS |</strong> Arrive early, bring your own towel + flip-flops, swim cap for lap pool</p></div></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><h2 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE VISITING SZECHENYI BATHS</h2><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><br></p><h3 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">WHERE ARE SZÉCHENYI BATHS, AND HOW TO GET THERE</h3><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Visiting Budapest on a weekend vacation? Or planning to spend a little more time exploring the <a href="https://www.thecommonwanderer.com/blog/things-to-do-in-budapest-hungary" target="_blank">best of this incredible city</a>? Either way, you’re going to want to visit Széchenyi Baths!</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The baths are located in City Park (Városliget) in the northeast of the city. Fortunately, the baths are located very close to the centre of town, and all the main attractions that Budapest has to offer.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">To <a href="https://www.google.com/maps/place/Sz%C3%A9chenyi+Thermal+Bath/@47.5076132,19.0561149,14z/data=!4m5!3m4!1s0x0:0xcbc0c308b68d2412!8m2!3d47.5186568!4d19.0823791" target="_blank">get to Széchenyi baths</a>, take the historic M1 (Millennium Underground) to Széchenyi fürdő station, a 2-minute walk from the entrance. The line runs from Vörösmarty tér through Deák Ferenc tér, Opera, and Heroes Square (Hősök tere).</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">…</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">If you’re keen to walk off some food/booze calories, it’s a super easy stroll to Széchenyi Baths.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">From Deak Ferenc Ter, you can walk the length of Andrassy Utca (Street), a UNESCO World Heritage site, and admire the beautiful, tree-lined boulevard, before arriving at Heroes Square.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">From Heroes Square, continue straight across the bridge before arriving at Széchenyi Baths on your left. Overall, the walk from the Deak Ferenc Ter and surrounds should take under an hour.</p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><h3 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">HOW TO PURCHASE SZÉCHENYI THERMAL BATHS ENTRANCE TICKETS</h3><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Tickets can be <a href="https://www.getyourguide.com/budapest-l29/szechenyi-spa-full-day-entrance-pass-t4139/?cmp=Szechenyi_Guide&partner_id=C8WLDEM&placement=content-middle&utm_medium=online_publisher" target="_blank">purchased online</a> prior to your visit, or at the ticket office upon entry to the baths (there are two entry points - Állatkerti Korut and Kós Károly Setany).</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">However, we suggest joining this wildly popular <a href="https://www.getyourguide.com/budapest-l29/szechenyi-spa-full-day-entrance-pass-t4139/?cmp=Szechenyi_Guide&partner_id=C8WLDEM&placement=content-middle&utm_medium=online_publisher" target="_blank">tour of Szechenyi Baths</a>, including a traditional Palinka tasting. </p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">It gets you skip-the-line access which, trust us, is needed, especially in summer. Plus, you’ll get to try Hungary’s most famous (and notorious) liqueur. </p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The Széchenyi ticket price is as follows (2025 prices):</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Weekday ticket with locker</span> | HUF 11,900 (€30)</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Weekend ticket with a locker (Fri, Sat, Sun)</span> | HUF 13,500 (€34)</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Good morning Budapest ticket (entrance until 9 am)</span> | HUF 9,900 (€24)</p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Cabins are an additional HUF 1,000–1,200 (€2.50–3)</p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><blockquote><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><strong>BOOK |</strong> Your <a href="https://www.getyourguide.com/budapest-l29/szechenyi-spa-full-day-entrance-pass-t4139/?cmp=Szechenyi_Guide&partner_id=C8WLDEM&placement=content-middle&utm_medium=online_publisher" target="_blank">Szechenyi Baths tickets</a> (+ Palinka tasting) in advance</p></blockquote><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">* Note that due to inflation, prices have almost doubled as of 2025</p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><h4 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">CAN I USE THE BUDAPEST CARD AT SZÉCHENYI BATHS?</h4><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">If you’re not sure what on earth we’re talking about, the Budapest Card is Hungary’s official city tourism pass.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">They’re valid for 72 hours (perfect for a city break!) and give you free public transport, plus free and/or discounted entry to the city’s main highlights, like most of the galleries and museums, for example.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">It’s well worth it if you plan to do plenty of sightseeing while you’re in town — and you can also use the Budapest Card to get <span style="text-decoration:underline"><em>20% off your entry ticket at the Széchenyi thermal baths</em></span><em>. </em>Winning!</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><br></p><blockquote><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><strong>BUY |</strong> <a your Budapest Card here</a></p></blockquote><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><br></p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><strong>NOTE |</strong> It is not recommended that children under 14 swim in thermal waters.   <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><h3 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">EARLY MORNING IS THE BEST TIME TO VISIT SZÉCHENYI BATHS</h3><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The <span style="text-decoration:underline">best time to visit Széchenyi baths is early morning</span> before the hordes of (other, ill-informed) tourists arrive! This means before 9 am, if not slightly earlier in the summer months (7:30 am is the sweet spot).</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">In Europe, especially during the peak seasons, tourist attractions get busy. Very busy. But if you’re out enjoying the attractions early in the morning while most people are still sleeping, you’ll have the place to yourself and enjoy a way better experience.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">And this is the case here at Széchenyi. </p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><span style="text-decoration:underline"><em>Arrive as early as possible</em></span> (even with sore heads from a big night at Szimpla Kert) and enjoy the beautiful baths all to yourself. Alternatively, arrive later in the day/evening when the crowds have left for the day. </p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">…</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">We highly recommend visiting the baths between May - October. The outside temperatures and longer hours of sunlight make the whole experience more enjoyable.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Although winter is a wonderful (and quieter) time to visit, getting to the outside pools when the temperature is low can ruin the vibe a little (trust us, your feet will freeeeeze!). That, and the position of the winter sun means the outdoor pools are only partially bathed in sun.</p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p></div>

</div></div><div class="sqs-block website-component-block sqs-block-website-component sqs-block-html html-block" data-block-css="["https://definitions.sqspcdn.com/website-component-definition/static-assets/website.components.html/45a223c2-0a7f-41e1-910b-7e4ed1931d30_973/website.components.html.styles.css"]" data-block-scripts="["https://definitions.sqspcdn.com/website-component-definition/static-assets/website.components.html/45a223c2-0a7f-41e1-910b-7e4ed1931d30_973/website.components.html.visitor.js"]" data-block-type="1337" data-definition-name="website.components.html" data-sqsp-block="text" data-website-component-id="yui_3_17_2_1_1642518515504_73993" id="block-yui_3_17_2_1_1642518515504_73993"><div class="sqs-block-content"><div class="sqs-text-block-container">
  
  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><h3 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">AN OVERVIEW OF THE SZECHENYI BATHS FACILITIES </h3><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Szechenyi is filled with everything you need for health and wellbeing, however, we’re not going to list out every facet of the baths, but rather just what’s important for visiting tourists.<br></p><h4 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">OUTDOOR POOLS</h4><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Szechenyi Baths are separated into two distinct sections, with the beautiful outdoor area being the most popular for visitors.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Here, there are three pools encased by the pastel yellow building, two heated immersion pools (one activity pool of 30 - 34 degrees, one thermal pool of 38 degrees), and the 50m swimming pool (26-28 degrees).</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The thermal pool is the best place to relax and enjoy the nostalgic atmosphere, especially in the winter, with the soothing warm waters providing perfect respite from the chilly air. Here, locals like to relax, read books or even play pool. In summer, though, it’s a different story.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Head for the activity pool for the cooler temperatures and the insanely strong whirlpool, and relax all day in the glorious sunshine.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">In summer, too, the outdoor area becomes a terrace for sunbathing or relaxing on the ornate gallery.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The 50m swimming pool is used for, you guessed it, swimming. You’ll need a cap to enter the pool, and most likely goggles if you’re really keen for a few laps.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Getting to the outdoor section can be a little bit of a struggle from the changing rooms. Just follow the signs to the pools, and follow your nose as far right (or left) as possible, at which point you’ll see a glass door that opens to the outdoor section. </p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">It is signposted, albeit quite poorly, but you’ll get there in the end.</p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><h4 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">INDOOR POOLS</h4><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The interior pools, while less awe-inspiring than the outdoor pools, are no less enjoyable.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">In total, there are 15 indoor pools ranging from 18 degrees to 40 degrees, of which a few are just not worth visiting unless you’re a regular. </p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Do you really want to do aqua aerobics in a 28-degree fitness pool? There’s also a 40-degree plunge pool (and 20-degree pool to cool off), as well as numerous sauna and steam rooms in this part of the baths.</p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><h4 data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></h4><h4 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">MASSAGE</h4><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">If the thermal pools aren’t enough, it’s also possible to get a massage at Szechenyi Baths.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">There is a range of massage types, from the aroma massage (20 mins: HUF 10,000) to the harmony aroma massage (45 mins: HUF 18,000).</p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><h4 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">ENTRANCE HALL DOME</h4><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">We have a thing for Budapest’s architecture and ornate finishings, and the entrance hall to Szechenyi is one of our faves. </p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The dome itself is the work of Hungarian artist Zsigmond Vajda, featuring motifs of Helios, the sun god, on his four horses, surrounded by zodiac signs. There are also water motifs based on Roman, Greek, Oriental and Egyptian mythologies.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The centaur statue and fountain in the middle of the entrance hall were our favourites though.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">So, when buying your tickets, make sure you stop, look up and around, and enjoy this entrance hall in all its glory!</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Prepare to be wowed as you walk in.<br></p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><h3 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">UNIQUE EXPERIENCES</h3><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><h4 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">SZECHENYI BATHS SPARTY</h4><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">What happens when you combine spas with a party? A Sparty, of course.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Each summer, Szechenyi comes alive at night for a huge set of <a href="https://www.getyourguide.com/budapest-l29/budapest-the-ultimate-late-night-spa-party-ticket-t386559/?cmp=Szechenyi_Guide&partner_id=C8WLDEM&placement=content-middle&utm_medium=online_publisher" target="_blank">parties</a>, where 2000 revellers party till dawn in the outdoor spa area.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">We have to admit, we’d have totally been up for it if we visited Budapest 10 years earlier, but this isn’t quite our thing now (we don’t have the bodies nor the drinking ability anymore!).</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">But, if you’ve come to Budapest for a good time, you can’t join a Sparty.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">More info can be found <a href="https://spartybooking.com/events-category/events/">here</a>.<br></p><blockquote><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"><strong>BOOK |</strong> Pre-purchase your <a href="https://www.getyourguide.com/budapest-l29/budapest-the-ultimate-late-night-spa-party-ticket-t386559/?cmp=Szechenyi_Guide&partner_id=C8WLDEM&placement=content-middle&utm_medium=online_publisher" target="_blank">Sparty ticket here</a></p></blockquote><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p><h4 style="white-space:pre-wrap;">SZECHENYI BATHS BEER SPA</h4><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">As much as we love Budapest, there are a few travel gimmicks around this city that make our millennial hearts cringe - those awful ‘all you can eat’ candy stores, the tacky tourist paraphernalia, the try-hard ‘ruin bars’ that are just lame bars trying to piggyback off something cool.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">We thought the beer spa at Szechenyi might have been one of those unfortunate gimmicks, but it actually seems really cool.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The beer spa includes a 45-minute beer spa that’s been infused with hops, malt and yeast, session, plus unlimited beer from your very own beer tap. The only sticking point is the price - it’s €50 per couple, or €30 per single, which is a little steep in a city like Budapest.</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Regardless, if you’re looking for something fun and different to do in the city, drink beer while bathing in beer at Szechenyi!</p><p class="" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Learn more <a href="https://thermalbeerspa.com/en/" target="_blank">here</a>.</p><p class="" data-rte-preserve-empty="true" style="white-space:pre-wrap;"></p></div>

<p>Fishermanâs Bastion is worth it, and for most people the ticket is not. Those two sentences are the whole guide, and the reason the second one surprises visitors is that the Bastion is the rare Budapest landmark where the famous view sits outside the turnstile. The terraces are open around the clock, every day of the year, for nothing. Only a strip of upper viewing level is ticketed, only between fixed hours, and only for 1,700 HUF (about $5) when it is.</p>
<p>So the useful question is not whether to come. It is when.</p>
<p><picture><source type="image/webp" srcset="/images/optimized/5ef944b8652f50d9fb6c248c-400.webp 400w, /images/optimized/5ef944b8652f50d9fb6c248c-768.webp 768w, /images/optimized/5ef944b8652f50d9fb6c248c-1440.webp 1440w" sizes="(max-width: 756px) calc(100vw - 2.3rem), 720px"><img src="/images/2026/09/fishermans-bastion-turrets-terrace-danube-panorama.jpg" alt="The white turrets and lookout terrace of Fishermanâs Bastion above the Buda hillside, with the Danube and the Pest rooftops behind" width="1600" height="1063" decoding="async"></picture>
<em>Photo: Jakub HaÅun, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons</em></p>
<h2 id="the-verdict-and-the-hour-it-depends-on">The verdict, and the hour it depends on</h2>
<p>The tourist-trap charge does not survive contact with the place. Almost everyone who comes here leaves happy, and the small minority who do not are complaining about one thing, consistently: the crowd. The square fills from late morning, the coach groups stack up through the afternoon, and the grievance that follows is hardly ever about the building.</p>
<p>Come between sunrise and 9:00 and you get the monument on the terms it was designed for: pale stone, an empty arcade, the Parliament across the water with the light behind you rather than in your lens. Come at 14:00 in July and you get a queue for a photo of a queue.</p>
<p>The evening is the other good answer, and it is the one people miss. When the ticket window shuts, the whole Bastion reverts to being free, and the city turns its floodlights on. The Chain Bridge, the Parliament and the GellÃ©rt Hill silhouette are all lit by then. You are paying nothing and looking at the better version.</p>

<h2 id="the-sunrise-arithmetic-which-is-better-than-it-sounds">The sunrise arithmetic, which is better than it sounds</h2>
<p>Here is a piece of scheduling nobody advertises. Budapestâs latest sunrise of the year is 07:31, from 28 December to 6 January. The gate never starts charging before 09:00. Which means:</p>
<p><strong>Sunrise at Fishermanâs Bastion is free. Every single day of the year.</strong> There is no season, no exception, no ticket window that opens early. Early-morning light on the Bastion costs nothing.</p>
<p>Sunset is the opposite story, and it changes with the calendar. From the spring clock change at the end of March until 31 May, the ticket window shuts at 19:00 and the sun sets after it, so sunset is free as well: 19:14 on 1 April, 20:33 on 31 May. On 1 June the window stretches to 21:00 and sunset falls back inside it. From October the sun is down long before 19:00, so the free evening window opens onto floodlit city rather than golden light.</p>
<p>Practical translation: <strong>in April and May you can have both ends of the day for nothing.</strong> In midsummer, pay if you want the turrets at sunset. In winter, do not bother waiting for 19:00 for the light, because there will not be any, but do wait for it if you want the lit city and an empty deck.</p>
<p><em>Sunrise times for Budapest read on <a href="https://www.timeanddate.com/sun/hungary/budapest">timeanddate.com</a> on 3 October 2026, December 2026 and January 2027 tables.</em></p>

<h2 id="what-you-are-actually-looking-at">What you are actually looking at</h2>
<p>Frigyes Schulek built the Bastion between 1895 and 1902, as part of the millennium works that reshaped the Castle District for Hungaryâs thousandth birthday. It is a viewing terrace wearing the costume of a fortress. No army ever held it, no siege was ever fought from it, and the crenellations have never done a dayâs work.</p>
<p>The seven turrets stand for the seven Magyar tribes who settled the Carpathian Basin in 895. The name comes from the fishermenâs guild said to have defended this stretch of medieval wall, a story the operator itself files under legend rather than record, which is a remarkably sober note for a monument of this size to strike.</p>
<p>St Stephen sits on his horse in the middle of it, facing the church rather than the river, which is the detail most visitors photograph without noticing. Below the ramparts there is a small chapel dedicated to St Michael. It is not covered by the Bastion ticket and currently holds no exhibition.</p>
<h2 id="the-restaurant-is-not-the-bastion">The restaurant is not the Bastion</h2>
<p>Inside the walls there is a restaurant called HalÃ¡szbÃ¡stya, and it is a separate business from the monument: run by a private company, with its own booking system at halaszbastya.eu. <p><strong>The lower terrace is wheelchair accessible</strong> by ramp from SzenthÃ¡romsÃ¡g tÃ©r, and the paths at that level are close to flat. <strong>The upper towers are not</strong>, and there is no lift to them, which means the ticketed half of the monument is unavailable to wheelchair users and the free half is the one that works.</p>
<p>The surrounding streets and the Castle courtyards are cobbled, and the cobbles are the real obstacle rather than the Bastion itself. SzenthÃ¡romsÃ¡g tÃ©r has been resurfaced and is manageable. Getting off the bus there leaves about 22 meters to cover.</p>
<p>There is a public toilet near the Bastion, on the SzenthÃ¡romsÃ¡g tÃ©r side, with an accessible cubicle. It charges a small fee and keeps its own hours.</p>
<p>Small dogs on a lead and muzzled are welcome, as are guide dogs. Large dogs are not, on a terrace that sees over half a million people a year.</p>
<h2 id="what-to-put-either-side-of-it">What to put either side of it</h2>
<p>The Bastion is a twenty minute visit that most people stretch to forty. It is the anchor of a Castle Hill morning rather than the morning itself.</p>
<p><strong><a href="/matthias-church-budapest-secrets-local-review/" title="Matthias Church Budapest: A Local's Review of the Secrets Inside">Matthias Church</a></strong> is the building the Bastion wraps around, and it is a genuinely separate ticket: 3,400 HUF (about $11) for an adult, 2,700 HUF concession, 9,500 HUF for a family of two adults and up to six children, with under-sixes free and an audioguide at 1,600 HUF. The tower is booked separately, by timed slot, with 197 steps and no lift. Two different ticket points stand a few meters apart up here selling very different things at very different prices, so read the sign before you join a line.</p>
<p><strong><a href="/labyrinth-of-buda-castle/" title="Labyrinth of Buda Castle: What It Costs and What You Actually See">The Labyrinth under Buda Castle</a></strong> is five minutes away and the natural counterweight: cold, dark and underground after all that open sky.</p>
<p><strong><a href="/budapest-hospital-in-the-rock-insider-guide/" title="Hospital in the Rock Budapest: An Insider's Guide">The Hospital in the Rock</a></strong> is the serious one on this hill, a wartime hospital and nuclear bunker in the same rock, and it is the visit people remember longest.</p>
<p><strong><a href="/liberty-statue-gellert-hill-budapest-guide/" title="Liberty Statue and GellÃ©rt Hill Budapest: The Complete Guide">The Liberty Statue on GellÃ©rt Hill</a></strong> gives you the reverse angle across the river, from higher up and for free.</p>

Zufahrtsregeln der Umweltzone

Bis auf Weiteres gilt eine Zufahrtsbeschränkung für Diesel-Fahrzeuge mit den Abgasnormen Diesel, Euro 4/IV und schlechter in der Münchner Umweltzone (inklusive Mittlerer Ring).

  • Lieferverkehr und Anwohner*innen sind durch Beschilderung von der Zufahrtsbeschränkung für Diesel-Fahrzeuge ausgenommen.
  • Weitere Ausnahmen gibt es zum Beispiel für Handwerker*innen, Schichtdienstleistende, Menschen mit Behinderung oder Pflegerische Dienste. Details zu den Ausnahmen finden Sie im folgenden Abschnitt  „Ausnahmen und Ausnahmegenehmigungen“.

Diesel-Kraftfahrzeuge mit der Abgasnorm 5/V oder besser, Benzin-Fahrzeuge oder Fahrzeuge mit anderen Antriebsarten dürfen die Münchner Umweltzone (inklusive Mittlerer Ring) befahren, wenn sie eine grüne Umweltplakette haben.

Im nächsten Abschnitt finden Sie eine Kurzübersicht zu den Ausnahmen. Mit einem Klick auf das Pfeil-Zeichen sehen Sie weitere Details.

Kurzübersicht zu den geltenden Ausnahmen

  • Diesel Euro 6/VI und Fahrzeuge mit entsprechender Hardwarenachrüstung
  • Menschen mit bestimmten Behinderungen (siehe Ausnahmekonzept, Allgemeinverfügung, 1.2, n. & o.)
  • Einsatzkräfte (Krankenwagen, Polizei)

Die gesetzlichen Ausnahmen beruhen auf dem Anhang 3 der 35. BImSchV und § 47 BImSchG. Weitere Informationen zu den Ausnahmen entnehmen Sie dem Ausnahmekonzept. Dieses finden Sie unter dem Link im nächsten Abschnitt "Ausnahmekonzept".

  • Anwohner*innen und Lieferverkehr
  • Taxen, Fahrzeuge im Mietwagenverkehr
  • Zu- und Abfahrt für Linienverkehr zum Zentralen Omnibusbahnhof (ZOB)
  • Medizinische Notfälle
  • Bestattungsfahrzeuge
  • Inhaber*innen eines Münchner Handwerker-Parkausweises (siehe Ausnahmekonzept, Allgemeinverfügung)
  • Soziale und pflegerische Hilfsdienste
  • Schichtdienstleistende und weitere Personen, für Fahrten zur Ausübung ihrer Berufstätigkeit und denen das Ausweichen auf den Öffentlichen Personennahverkehr nicht möglich oder zumutbar ist
  • Zu- und Abfahrt zur Großmarkthalle, zum Autoreisezug (Ostbahnhof), zur Parkharfe Olympiastadion und zum Campingplatz Thalkirchen

Benzin-Fahrzeuge oder Fahrzeuge mit anderen Antriebsarten dürfen die um den Mittleren Ring erweiterte Umweltzone befahren, wenn sie eine grüne Umweltplakette haben.

Weitere Informationen zu den Ausnahmen inklusive einer Lesefassung der Allgemeinverfügung entnehmen Sie dem Ausnahmekonzept. Dieses finden Sie unter dem Link im nächsten Abschnitt "Ausnahmekonzept".

Die Allgemeinverfügung finden Sie hier. Die erste Änderung der Allgemeinverfügung finden Sie hier. Die zweite Änderung der Allgemeinverfügung finden Sie hier.

Wer nicht unter die unter A. genannten "Gesetzlich vorgegebene Ausnahmen" oder unter B. aufgeführten "Pauschale Ausnahmen per Beschilderung und Allgemeinverfügung" fällt, kann unter nachfolgendem Link einen Antrag auf Einzelausnahmegenehmigung stellen. Bitte beachten Sie auch hier die rechtliche Grundlage des § 1 Absatz 2 der 35. BImSchV.

Antragsberechtigt sind zum Beispiel Fahrten zur/für:

  • Reparatur und Erhalt betriebsnotwendiger Anlagen
  • Behebung von Gebäudeschäden
  • Versorgung der Bevölkerung mit lebensnotwendigen Gütern
     

Oder auch Fahrzeuge für folgende Zwecke:

  • Spezialfahrzeuge mit hohen Anschaffungskosten und geringer Fahrleistung
  • Fahrzeuge mit Spezialumbauten für Schwerbehinderte
  • Fahrzeuge für regelmäßige Arztbesuche
  • Private Härtefälle
  • Fahrten zur Aufrechterhaltung von Fertigungs- und Produktionsprozessen
  • Belieferung von Veranstaltungen mit Veranstaltungslogistik und -technik

Bei Fragen zur Beantragung einer Einzelausnahmen wenden Sie sich bitte an ausnahmeumweltzone.kvr@muenchen.de

Weitere Informationen zu den Ausnahmen finden Sie im Ausnahmekonzept. Dieses finden Sie unter dem Link im nächsten Abschnitt "Ausnahmekonezpt".

Weitere Maßnahmen zur Verbesserung der Luft

Seit dem 20. Oktober 2025 gilt die neunte Fortschreibung des Münchner Luftreinhalteplans.
Darin sind unter anderem folgende Maßnahmen vorgesehen: Tempo 30 auf beiden Seiten der Landshuter Allee zwischen der Arnulfstraße im Süden und dem Toni-Merkens-Weg im Norden sowie eine angepasste Ampelschaltung an der Moosacher Straße.

Häufige Fragen (FAQs)

Die Abgasnorm steht auf dem Fahrzeugschein unter Punkt 14.

Achtung! Die Grüne Umweltplakette mit der Ziffer 4 an der Windschutzscheibe ist nicht gleichzusetzen mit der Abgasnorm. Neuere Dieselfahrzeuge der Abgasnorm 6/VI verfügen ebenfalls über eine Grüne Umweltplakette mit der Ziffer 4, diese sind jedoch von der Zufahrtsbeschränkung befreit.

 

Zu den Anwohner*innen, die per Beschilderung von der Zufahrtsbeschränkung für Diesel-Fahrzeuge (Euro 4/IV und schlechter) ausgenommen sind, zählen alle Bürger*innen, die innerhalb der um den Mittleren Ring erweiterten Umweltzone wohnhaft gemeldet sind (inklusive Zweitwohnsitz).

Bitte beachten: Das gilt nur für Fahrzeuge mit grüner Plakette. Für Fahrzeuge mit gelber oder roter Plakette können Anwohner*innen weiterhin gebührenpflichtige Einzelausnahmen beantragen.

Für Straßen, die ausschließlich über den Mittleren Ring (B2R) erreicht oder verlassen werden können (zum Beispiel wegen Einbahnstraßenregelungen), ist die Befahrung des Mittleren Ring (B2R) auf dem kürzesten Weg erlaubt. Davon betroffen sind beispielsweise Oberaudorferstraße, Schloss-Berg-Straße, Einsteinstraße (westlich der Vogelweidestraße / Truderinger Straße bis hin zum Leuchtenbergring). Dass bedeutet, dass die um den Mittleren Ring (B2R) erweiterte Umweltzone zwar kurzfristig befahren werden darf, aber an der nächsten Möglichkeit wieder verlassen werden muss.

Unter Lieferverkehr ist der geschäftsmäßige Transport von Waren zu verstehen, wenn diese zu Gewerbetreibenden oder Kund*innen innerhalb der Umweltzone geliefert oder von dort abgeholt werden.

Ein Nachweis kann hierbei ein Lieferschein, Auftragsbestätigung oder Liefergegenstand sein. Wichtig ist, dass der Hauptzweck der Fahrt der Lieferung der Ware dient.

Handwerker*innen mit einem Handwerker-Parkausweis für das Stadtgebiet München können in die, um den Mittleren Ring erweiterte, Umweltzone unbefristet fahren.

Handwerker*innen ohne Parkausweis können zur Lieferung ihrer Waren und Dienstleistung weiterhin die um den Mittleren Ring erweiterte Umweltzone befahren. Voraussetzung hierfür ist ein Handwerkerfahrzeug als Werkstattwagen oder zum Transport von Werkzeug und Materialien. Zudem muss der Handwerksbetrieb in der Handwerksordnung (Anlage A oder B) aufgelistet sein oder es sich um eine vergleichbare Tätigkeit handeln (zum Beispiel Wartungsdienst, Installation Großgeräte).

Für Schichtdienstleistende, Sozial- und Pflegedienste sowie weitere Personen, die zur Ausübung ihrer Tätigkeit nicht auf Alternativen, insbesondere auf den Öffentlichen Personennahverkehr, ausweichen können gilt eine Sonderregelung.

Weitere Informationen finden Sie auf der Seite: „Ausnahmegenehmigungen zum Befahren der Umweltzone“ unter „Fragen & Antworten“.

Schwerbehinderte Menschen der Merkzeichen „G“,  „aG“, „H“ und „BI“, Inhaber*innen des orangen und blauen Parkausweises und Personen die diese fahren, sind von den Einschränkungen ausgenommen.

Wer diese Voraussetzungen nicht erfüllt, kann nach Einzelfallprüfung gegebenenfalls eine Ausnahmegenehmigung erhalten.

Das Stadtgebiet innerhalb des Mittleren Rings ist sehr gut mit den öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln zu erreichen.

Auch die Nutzung von P+R-Parkplätzen, also die Kombination von Auto und öffentlichem Verkehr, kann eine Möglichkeit darstellen. Gleiches trifft auf das Fahrrad zu.

Für Situationen, in denen ein Auto zwingend nötig ist, können Fahrzeuge der verschiedenen Carsharing-Anbieter, privates Carsharing oder Mitfahrzentralen eine Lösung sein.

Fahrzeuge der Abgasnormen Euro 4/IV und Euro 5/V, die über sogenannte Stickoxid-Minderungssysteme mit hoher Minderungsleistung zur Einhaltung eines Emissionswertes von weniger als 270 Milligramm Stickoxid je Kilometer Fahrt verfügen, sind gemäß § 47 Absatz 4a Satz 2 Nummer 2 BImSchG von Verkehrsverboten ausgenommen.

Um zu erfahren, ob für Ihr Fahrzeug ein Stickoxid-Minderungssystem mit hoher Minderungsleistung zugelassen ist, wenden Sie sich bitte an den Fahrzeughersteller oder eine Fachwerkstatt.

Zusätzliche Informationen zur Allgemeinen Betriebserlaubnis für NOx-Minderungssysteme erhalten Sie auf der Seite des Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt .

Kontrolle der Zufahrtsbeschränkung

Die Zufahrtsbeschränkung für Diesel-Fahrzeuge (Euro 4/IV und schlechter) wird im Rahmen der üblichen Verkehrskontrollen im fließenden Verkehr durch die Polizei vorgenommen.

Ergänzend prüft die kommunale Verkehrsüberwachung bei Kontrollen des ruhenden Verkehrs sowie im Rahmen von Geschwindigkeitskontrollen die Vorgaben der Umweltzone.

Für die Kontrollen sind Aktionstage und -wochen vorgesehen, bei denen gezielt in Hinblick auf die Zufahrtsberechtigung in die Umweltzone kontrolliert wird.

Darüber hinaus wird im Zusammenhang mit der Vergabe von Anwohner-Parklizenzen die Abgasnorm geprüft.

Der Verstoß gegen die Zufahrtsbeschränkung für Diesel-Fahrzeuge (Euro 4/IV und schlechter) wird nach dem derzeit gültigen Bußgeldkatalog mit einem Bußgeld von 100 Euro geahndet. Rechtsgrundlage ist das Bundesimmissionsschutzgesetz. Zuzüglich Gebühren und Auslagen erwarten die Verkehrsteilnehmenden bei Missachtung der Vorschrift Kosten in Höhe von 128,50 Euro.

Es gibt keinen Punkteeintrag im Fahreignungsregister.

Information

Fragen zur Zufahrtsbeschränkung?

Individuelle Fragen zur Zufahrtsbeschränkung für Diesel-Fahrzeuge (Euro 4/IV und schlechter), zur persönlichen Betroffenheit oder zu den geltenden Ausnahmen können Sie an buergeranfragen.rku@muenchen.de senden.

Bei Fragen zur Beantragung einer Einzelausnahmen wenden Sie sich bitte an ausnahmeumweltzone.kvr@muenchen.de.

Ergänzende Informationen

Zwei Luftschadstoffe stehen im Fokus der Luftreinhalteplanung: Stickstoffdioxid (NO2) und Feinstaub (PM10, PM2,5).

Die relevanten lufthygienischen Grenzwerte für Feinstaub werden bereits seit 2012 (PM10) und seit 2015 (PM2,5) im Stadtgebiet eingehalten.

Der vorgegebene Jahresmittelgrenzwert für Stickstoffdioxid von 40 µg/m³ werden seit 2024 im gesamten Stadtgebiet eingehalten. Die aktuellen Stickstoffdioxid-Messergebnisse werden regelmäßig durch die Stadt München und das Landesamt für Umwelt veröffentlicht.

Die Europäische Union hat mit der "Richtlinie 2008/50/EG über Luftqualität und saubere Luft für Europa" vom 21. Mai 2008 für verschiedene Luftschadstoffe verbindliche Grenzwerte sowie Zielwerte festgelegt.

Damit soll die Verschmutzung so reduziert werden, dass die schädlichen Auswirkungen auf die menschliche Gesundheit und die Umwelt möglichst gering sind.

Die relevantesten Schadstoffe in Zusammenhang mit Luftreinhalteplänen sind Feinstaub (PM10) und Stickstoffdioxid (NO2). Die Richtlinie ist in den Mitgliedsstaaten in nationales Recht überführt worden.

In Deutschland ist die Richtlinie durch das achte Gesetz zur Änderung des Bundes-Immissionsschutzgesetzes sowie durch die 39. Verordnung zur Durchführung des Bundes-Immissionsschutzgesetzes (39. BImSchV) umgesetzt worden. In der 39. BImSchV sind alle Grenz- und Zielwerte für Luftschadstoffe festgelegt, die von den Bundesländern und Kommunen eingehalten werden müssen. Zudem enthält sie Vorgaben zur Ermittlung der Schadstoffbelastung.

2024 wurde die EU-Luftqualitätsrichtlinie erneuert. Die EU-Richtlinie ist vom Bund bis spätestens Dezember 2026 in nationales Gesetz zu überführen.

Ein Schwerpunkt der neuen EU-Luftqualitätsrichtlinie sind die strengeren Grenzwerte ab 2030. Nachfolgend ein Ausschnitt zu den verschärften Grenzwerten, die für die Stadt München von besonderer Bedeutung sind.

Stickstoffdioxid-Grenzwert:

  • bisheriger Jahresmittelgrenzwert 40 µg/m³
    neuer Jahresmittelgrenzwert 20 µg/m³
  • bisheriger Stundenmittelgrenzwert 200 µg/m³ (erlaubte Überschreitung: 18 Stunden pro Jahr)
    neuer Stundenmittelgrenzwert 200 µg/m³ (erlaubte Überschreitung: 3 Stunden pro Jahr)
  • neuer 24-Stundenmittelgrenzwert 50 µg/m³ (erlaubte Überschreitung: 18 Tagen im Jahr)

Feinstaub-Grenzwerte:

  • PM10 bisheriger Jahresmittelgrenzwert 40 µg/m³
    neuer Jahresmittelgrenzwert 20 µg/m³
  • PM10 bisheriger 24-Stundenmittelgrenzwert 50 µg/m³ (erlaubte Überschreitung: 35 Tagen im Jahr)
    neuer 24-Stundenmittelgrenzwert 45 µg/m³ (erlaubte Überschreitung: 18 Tagen im Jahr)
  • PM2,5 bisheriger Jahresmittelgrenzwert 25 µg/m³
    neuer Jahresmittelgrenzwert für 10 µg/m³
  • PM2,5 neuer 24-Stundenmittelgrenzwert 25 µg/m³ (erlaubte Überschreitung: 18 Tagen im Jahr)

Die vorläufige Jahreskurzauswertung des Landesamt für Umwelt für 2025 zeigt, dass bereits jetzt im gesamten Stadtgebiet die neuen Feinstaub-Grenzwerte (PM10, PM2,5) eingehalten werden können. Sofern keine unvorhergesehene Entwicklung eintritt, ist davon auszugehen, dass die neuen Feinstaub-Grenzwerte für München keinen Reaktion erfordern.

Anders ist das bei der Verschärfung des Stickstoffdioxid-Grenzwerts. Aufgrund der bevorstehenden Halbierung des Werts besteht für die kommenden Jahre weiterhin großer Handlungsbedarf. Die Stadt München ist weiterhin verpflichtet, die eingeführten Maßnahmen beizubehalten und Strategien zu entwickeln, um die neuen Jahresmittelgrenzwerte bis 2030 einzuhalten.

    Discover benefits

    Starting September 8, 2026, admission to the Kunsthistorisches Museum will be available exclusively during reserved time slots. We recommend making a reservation in advance through the online shop.

    Tickets purchased before September 8 can be used flexibly during regular opening hours. Booking an additional time slot is not required.

    Your online ticket will be sent by email to the address provided by you. Please also check your spam folder.

    The time slot ticket entitles you to a single entry on the selected visit date and at the selected time. There is no time limit on your visit to the museum.

    Given the growing number of fake websites, there is a risk of purchasing counterfeit tickets that may not be accepted on site. Therefore, please only purchase your tickets from official ticket websites. Original tickets for the Kunsthistorisches Museum are only available online at https://shop.khm.at/tickets

    All about your visit

    Leave your outerwear, umbrellas, bags and other items at the cloakroom free of charge. There are also lockers available for storage.

    Please note that the Kunsthistorisches Museum does not offer luggage storage.

    We are happy to welcome our youngest guests and offer special programmes for children and teenagers. Children must be supervised during the entire visit.

    Our art educational offers for children

    Visitors with buggies are requested to contact the visitor service, who will be happy to assist you.

    If there are large numbers of visitors, we may restrict the number of buggies that can be taken into the exhibition rooms.

    Well-maintained toilets are available on levels 0, 0.5 and 1 during your visit. You can find the exact location on the floor plan.

    Use our café and restaurant for a break during your visit. The café and restaurant is open throughout the museum opening hours.

    Seating is available in the exhibition rooms, take a seat while viewing and experiencing the works of art.

    We ask for your understanding that for safety reasons animals (except assistance animals) are not permitted.

    The Kunsthistorisches Museum offers a comprehensive barrier-free visitor experience with reduced admission, accessible infrastructure, specialised guided tours, tactile and auditory services and excellent inclusive initiatives for people with different needs.

It is drawn on a clock.</p>
<p>The most photographed viewpoint in the city costs 1,700 Ft at two in the afternoon and nothing at eight in the morning. It is the same stone, the same view, the same set of stairs. Only the hour is different.</p>
<h2 id="the-ticket-at-fishermans-bastion-only-applies-for-part-of-the-day">The ticket at Fishermanâs Bastion only applies for part of the day</h2>
<p><picture><source type="image/webp" srcset="/images/optimized/c8103347e03e3aa3c76d59b2-400.webp 400w, /images/optimized/c8103347e03e3aa3c76d59b2-768.webp 768w, /images/optimized/c8103347e03e3aa3c76d59b2-1440.webp 1440w" sizes="(max-width: 756px) calc(100vw - 2.3rem), 720px"><img src="/images/2026/08/fishermans-bastion-lower-terraces-stairs.jpg" alt="The grand staircase leading up to Fishermanâs Bastionâs lower terrace arcade in Budapest, with Matthias Churchâs tiled tower behind" width="1600" height="1067" decoding="async"></picture>
<em>Photo: <a href="https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Fisherman%27s_Bastion,_Budapest,_Hungary.jpg">Veronika Szappanos</a>, <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">CC BY-SA 4.0</a>, resized. The grand staircase and lower terrace arcade, free at every hour. Matthias Churchâs tower stands behind it and is a separate, ticketed building.</em></p>
<!-- image-licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 | author: Veronika Szappanos (Veronika.szappanos) | source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Fisherman%27s_Bastion,_Budapest,_Hungary.jpg | retrieved: 2026-08-18 -->
<p>Fishermanâs Bastion has two halves and they are priced differently.</p>
<p>The lower terraces, the balconies and the long run of hillside stairs, roughly 140 metres of them, are free all year at every hour. That is where the view most people have seen actually comes from. Nobody checks a ticket there and nobody ever has.</p>
<p>The upper towers and upper terraces are ticketed at 1,700 Ft for an adult, and this is the part worth understanding properly, because the charge does not run all day.</p>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>Outside those hours the operatorâs own position is that visiting the Bastion, lower and upper towers and terraces alike, is free.</p>
<aside data-hu-ad="1" data-pagefind-ignore aria-label="Advertisement"><span class="hu-ad-label">Advertisement</span><div class="hu-ad-space"><ins class="hu-ad-pending" data-ad-client="ca-pub-3645638175832007" data-ad-slot="2803598552"></ins></div></aside><p>In August, that means the upper towers cost nothing before 09:00 and nothing after 21:00. Sunrise on the Bastion is free, and it is also when the arcade is empty and the light is coming across Pest towards you rather than glaring back off the river. The expensive hours and the bad hours are the same hours. If you want the evening version of that trade rather than the morning one, we rank it against the other viewpoints in our guide to <a href="/amazing-sunset-spots-in-budapest/">Budapest sunset spots</a>.</p>
<p>Students with ID, children between 6 and 14 with ID, and EU seniors pay half. Children under six are free at any hour, as are visitors with a disability and one companion.</p>
<h3 id="three-days-a-year-when-the-whole-thing-is-free">Three days a year when the whole thing is free</h3>
<p>Fishermanâs Bastion charges nothing at all on 15 March, 20 August and 23 October, and again during the week between Christmas and New Year. If your trip covers 20 August you get the towers for nothing on the same day the city puts on <a href="/budapest-august-20-fireworks-best-viewing-spots-guide/">its fireworks</a>.</p>
<h2 id="the-one-that-quietly-stopped-being-free">The one that quietly stopped being free</h2>
<p>St Stephenâs Basilica is the entry most worth correcting, because the amount of money involved is not small and the mistake is still being repeated.</p>
<p>Entry has been ticketed since 1 December 2025. The operator states plainly that every individual and group visitor is required to buy a ticket and that it is checked at the entrance.</p>

<p>Children under six enter free. A family ticket for two adults and two children under 12 is 7,300 Ft for the hall and 20,400 Ft combined. Discounted tickets have to be bought at the ticket office beside the Basilica, on presentation of whatever card qualifies you.</p>
<p>The Basilica spent years as a church you could walk into for the price of whatever you dropped in the box, which is why the change catches people. Arriving with a few hundred forint and a plan to donate it now ends at a ticket desk.</p>
<aside data-hu-ad="2" data-pagefind-ignore aria-label="Advertisement"><span class="hu-ad-label">Advertisement</span><div class="hu-ad-space"><ins class="hu-ad-pending" data-ad-client="ca-pub-3645638175832007" data-ad-slot="2803598552"></ins></div></aside><p>The church hall opens 09:00 to 18:00 Monday to Saturday and 13:00 to 18:00 on Sunday. The terrace and treasury run 09:00 to 19:00 daily. Weekend weddings can close the hall to visitors, which the operator warns about itself.</p>
<h2 id="the-fortress-park-nobody-charges-for">The fortress park nobody charges for</h2>
<p>The Citadella on top of GellÃ©rt Hill spent years fenced off and came back in April 2026. The part that matters for a free day is that the park inside the fortress walls, more than 6,000 square metres of it, is open to everyone at no charge.</p>
<p>It stays open until midnight from April to October, and until 22:00 from November to March. A free viewpoint that is open at midnight in August is an unusual thing for a capital city to have.</p>
<p>What is ticketed is the exhibition in the western gun tower, at 4,900 Ft for an adult and 2,450 Ft for students, under-26s and seniors between 62 and 70. It runs 10:00 to 18:00 most days and 12:00 to 20:00 on Fridays. Under-6s, over-70s and visitors with a disability plus one companion go in free.</p>
<p>You can have the entire hill without that ticket, and most people who go up do exactly that. The 360 degree view over the Danube and the bridges is the reason to climb, and it belongs to the park rather than to the exhibition.</p>
<p>Two things to know before you set off. The climb is steep, steeper than it looks from the bottom, and people regularly underestimate it in summer heat; a bus runs to the top for the price of a transport fare if the walk is not appealing. And the toilets up there are charged, which is worth a couple of coins in your pocket on a day built around spending nothing.</p>

The park is free. The buildings in it are mostly not.</p>

<p>Free walking tours are a separate case: they are free to join and run on tips, and what people actually hand over at the end is a real cost rather than a notional one. We have put numbers on that in our guide to <a href="/budapest-walking-tour-free-vs-paid/">free versus paid walking tours</a>.</p>
<h2 id="building-a-day-out-of-it">Building a day out of it</h2>
<p>A workable free day, using only things above: start at the Bastion before 09:00 while the upper towers are still free, walk down through the Castle District, cross the Chain Bridge on foot, follow the Danube Promenade past the Shoes memorial, then take the afternoon on Margaret Island. If you still have legs at the end of it, go up GellÃ©rt Hill for the evening and stay in the park until it gets dark. In August the park does not close until midnight.</p>
<p>That is a full day in a capital city for the price of a transport ticket. The trick is knowing which hour you are standing in front of each gate.</p>

You can walk the whole hill, the walls and the park, and take the view over the Danube and the bridges, without buying anything.</p></details><details data-astro-cid-3blcfnl5><summary data-astro-cid-3blcfnl5>What is the cheapest way to get up GellÃ©rt Hill?</summary><p data-astro-cid-3blcfnl5>Walking is free and it is a genuine climb, steep enough that plenty of people who set off on foot wish they had not.
